verification_questions: Does the source assert stdio MCP servers MUST log to stderr (not stdout)?

verification_answers: Yes — F3.1 line 94: 'Stdio MCP servers must direct all log output to stderr. Logging to stdout corrupts the JSON-RPC framing on the transport.'

Source-quote at line 96 (Anthropic Debugging docs, modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/tools/debugging): 'Local MCP servers should not log messages to stdout, as this will interfere with protocol operation.' Note: the underlying Anthropic doc uses 'should not' (a strong recommendation, RFC-2119 SHOULD NOT), not a literal RFC 'MUST NOT'. The claim text uses 'must' as a lowercase imperative, which is acceptable paraphrase but worth flagging — the spec language is 'should not'.
Yes — claim text reproduces the framing-corruption rationale.
critiques.notes: Slight calibration issue: the Anthropic Debugging guidance is 'should not log to stdout' (engineering-imperative), not RFC-2119 'MUST NOT'. The claim's lowercase 'must' is a reasonable paraphrase but the Synthesizer should not represent this as a literal protocol MUST — it is a Debugging-guide imperative anchored on the practical consequence (stream corruption). Confidence downgraded to medium because the universal quantifier 'must' is stronger than the source's language. Substance is verified; the prescriptive force matches the source's intent (do not do this), even if the modal verb differs.

notable_findings: F5.4 NO CONSENSUS claim (C-0349) survives targeted secondary search. The note enumerates 5 source-categories surveyed and finds the closest analogue (microservice circuit-breaker) while explicitly noting it does not transfer. The no-consensus call is defensible.

Three fallback-surface options (C-0352 stderr banner / C-0353 mcp-events.jsonl / C-0354 agent-level ack) are genuinely distinct — different surface, different persistence, different operator-discovery path. Not synonyms.

C-0313 (stdio MUST log to stderr): claim uses 'must' but Anthropic Debugging source uses 'should not'. Substance verified; modal force slightly over-stated. Confidence downgraded to medium. Synthesizer should not represent this as RFC-2119 MUST.

Fast.io ping parameters (30s/2-5s/3-failure) are single-vendor pattern (medium confidence ceiling) but consistent with industry liveness-probe defaults. C-0295, C-0296, C-0361 form an internally consistent triple.

OWASP MCP01 ranking (C-0333) is by-definition true given OWASP is the authority for the taxonomy. No cross-corroboration needed for the ranking itself; the recommendation language (C-0335) is verbatim-quoted.
